stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing multi-drug single-dose compliance packages. Which scenarios can fit the current policy's Schedule II/III maintenance-medication allowance, assuming all other requirements are satisfied? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Stable buprenorphine Schedule III maintenance therapy when otherwise compliant
A three-day acute oxycodone course added only because it is Schedule II
An alprazolam dose placed in the package without checking any other packaging/dispensing requirements solely because it is Schedule IV
Daily methylphenidate used as a stable maintenance medication
Stable testosterone cypionate therapy treated as a maintenance medication

explanation.core_reasoning: Current Massachusetts policy permits qualifying Schedule II/III maintenance medications in multi-drug single-dose packages; acute status and other packaging requirements still matter.

choice_analysis.A: The policy can include qualifying S-III maintenance medication.
choice_analysis.B: The policy's expansion is for maintenance medication, not every acute C-II course.
choice_analysis.C: The stated S-II/III maintenance expansion does not erase other requirements.
choice_analysis.D: A Schedule II maintenance medication can fit the policy.
choice_analysis.E: Schedule III maintenance medication can fit.

related_facts: The policy was revised to remove an older categorical exclusion of S-II/III maintenance medications.
explanation.mpje_trap: Interpreting 'Schedule II/III allowed' as a blanket controlled-drug exemption.

reasoning_steps: Apply the compliance-packaging policy without erasing other rules
